$description: Console-side corpus for Jace's Layer 2 injection screen (spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-28-jace-input-guardrails-design.md). Reuses the EXACT schema of agentrail/guardrails/fixtures/injection_corpus.json so the two corpora stay comparable (injection.test.ts's Python cross-check shells out to agentrail.guardrails.policies.input_contract.screen_injection over every case body here and asserts agreement with detectInjection() !== null, so the TS and Python deny-lists cannot silently drift). The first 9 cases (ids unchanged) are seeded verbatim from that Python fixture: they are GitHub-issue-shaped bodies with an '## Acceptance criteria' checkbox section. The remaining cases are NEW and chat-shaped — a DM to Jace has no issue template, so this corpus adds the same attack families phrased as a chat message, plus negative controls: a developer legitimately discussing THIS guardrail feature, and ordinary work chat that happens to use trigger-adjacent words (secret, token, api key, merge, approve, review, bash) without forming an actual injection directive. 'reject' cases are prompt-injection probes; 'admit' cases MUST pass clean at every trust tier.

$shape.version: integer schema version; bump on any breaking shape change.
$shape.cases: array of case objects, each with the fields below.
$shape.case.id: stable, unique, machine-friendly identifier for the case (used in test ids and failure messages).
$shape.case.expect: the required screen verdict: 'reject' (injection probe: detectInjection() must find a match) or 'admit' (negative control: must screen clean at every trust tier).
$shape.case.category: coarse grouping for reporting: 'injection' for probes, 'negative_control' for messages that must still be admitted.
$shape.case.body: the raw message text fed to detectInjection() / screenInjection(). Chat-shaped cases have no Acceptance-criteria section — unlike the Python fixture's issue bodies, a chat message is not required to carry one.
$shape.case.note: human-readable explanation of what the case exercises (not asserted on; documentation only).
